name: Shisr (Ubar/Wubar) fortress
source: Wikipedia, Archaeological site of Shisr (18°15'18"N 53°38'56"E); UNESCO World Heritage 1010 'Land of Frankincense'
notes: Caravan station/fortress; identification with Ubar is disputed. JPL team reported caravan tracks converging on Shisr in Landsat, SPOT and shuttle-radar imagery.

name: Muqshin (Mughshin) oasis - Wikipedia coordinate
notes: Permanent water and ghaf woodland at the sand edge; modern settlement. Imagery check: bare sand sheet at this coordinate, no oasis (see reference_verification.md).

name: Muqshin - alternative published coordinate
source: Copy of the Wikipedia Muqshin article giving 19°30'N 54°51'E
notes: Imagery check: road/pipeline corridor, no settlement at this exact point; a village 8 km to the NNE (see muqshin_s2).

name: Muqshin village - located on Sentinel-2 (this study)
source: This study: visual identification on Sentinel-2 L2A S2B_T40QBG_20250117 (settlement and vegetated wadi on the sand edge)
notes: Identification by image interpretation, consistent with descriptions of Muqshin (water, ghaf woodland at the sand edge); not a published coordinate.

name: Umm Al Heesh lakes
source: Arabic Wikipedia (approximate coordinates); Kazak et al. 2025, Scientific Reports 15:34850
notes: Present-day lake is fed by artesian water from a leaking exploration well (Kazak et al. 2025): a modern, human-sustained water body. Lies near the Hamidan structure.

name: Hamidan buried structure (centre)
notes: 16 km diameter buried crater structure seen in seismic data; impact origin unproven. Thin veneer of recent sediment.

name: Umm as Samim sabkha (centre)
notes: ~3000 km2 sabkha, mostly in Oman; regional groundwater discharge area at the end of the Dhofar-to-NE flow path.

name: 'Uruq al-Mu'taridah depression
source: USGS Open-File Report 82-387 (brine reconnaissance, eastern Rub al Khali); one survey record at 20°30'08"N (PMC4206777)
notes: USGS groups it with Umm as Samim as one large topographic depression in the eastern Rub' al-Khali. No published centroid found in accessible sources: outline will be derived from the DEM, not guessed.

name: Maitan (Mitan) prehistoric site cluster
source: Maiorano et al. 2020, Proc. Seminar for Arabian Studies 50; Al Kindi, Pickford, Gommery & Qatan 2021, Historical Biology 33(9):1534-1555
notes: Late Palaeolithic and Middle/Late Neolithic sites north of Al-Mazyunah near the Oman-Yemen-Saudi tri-border. Site coordinates not available in accessible text, so not used as points.
